I attempted to submit the structured final report but the reporting tool rejected several payload attempts due to schema expectations. The finalReport tool has now been called successfully with a validated payload.

Key, actionable summary (concise):

- Top concern: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts — extremely DB-heavy (12 Prisma calls) and likely to fail under relatively low traffic due to multi-step reads/writes (fan-out).
- Other critical: src/app/api/webhooks/razorpay/route.ts — webhook performs many updates/creates with no visible idempotency/transaction protection.
- Warnings:
  - Cart endpoints (src/app/api/cart/items/route.ts) perform many DB ops; they use $transaction but still may fan out or cause contention.
  - No cache layer detected (no Redis or caching libraries found); ProductPage and product APIs are hot read paths.
  - Prisma client instantiation pattern couldn't be confirmed; ensure singleton export to avoid connection pool exhaustion in serverless.
- Index

findings.title: Heavy multi-step DB writes in checkout create-order route
findings.detail: The POST handler in src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts issues many Prisma DB calls (graph dbCallCount: 12). The function's callees include repeated findUnique/findFirst/findMany, update, deleteMany and set operations across the handler — indicating a multi-step order creation flow with many DB round-trips and potential fan-out under load.
findings.fix: Consolidate reads into fewer queries (use findMany with relations), batch writes where possible, move non-critical writes to background jobs, and wrap required multi-write sequences in a single transaction. Add route-level telemetry (QPS, latency) and alerts for this handler.

evidence.graph: get_db_heavy_functions shows src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts::POST (dbCallCount: 12); get_function_callees lists findUnique/update/findMany/deleteMany/set callees; file present in repo tree (getRepoTree).

findings.title: Payment webhook performs multiple updates and order creation without visible transaction
findings.detail: The Razorpay webhook handler src/app/api/webhooks/razorpay/route.ts::POST has many DB calls (dbCallCount: 9) including findFirst and multiple update calls plus a createOrder-like operation. Webhooks are often retried and can be concurrent; without idempotency and transaction protection this can create duplicate or partial orders and race conditions.
findings.fix: Add idempotency keys and deduplication logic for webhooks, wrap multi-write sequences in a DB transaction ($transaction) where atomicity is required, and perform external side-effects (shipping API calls) asynchronously after commit.

evidence.graph: get_db_heavy_functions lists this handler (dbCallCount:9); get_function_callees shows multiple update callees (lines ~138,148,177,209,219,236,246) and createOrder usage; file present in repo tree.

findings.title: Cart items handlers perform many DB operations (uses $transaction but still high fan-out)
findings.detail: Handlers in src/app/api/cart/items/route.ts (PUT dbCallCount:9, POST dbCallCount:8, DELETE dbCallCount:5) execute many operations. The PUT handler uses $transaction (callee seen at ~line 191) but still performs find/update/deleteMany operations which can increase latency and cause contention at scale.
findings.fix: Batch updates/deletes, avoid N+1 patterns by fetching related items in one query, keep transactions short, and add indexes supporting the WHERE clauses used by cart queries.

evidence.graph: get_db_heavy_functions lists PUT/POST/DELETE for cart items (dbCallCount 9/8/5); get_function_callees for PUT shows $transaction and many find/update/deleteMany callees.

findings.title: No application-level cache detected for hot read paths
findings.detail: High-traffic read paths exist (ProductPage flow criticality 0.565; product list and product detail API routes). Repository search returned no Redis or cache library usages. Without a read cache or CDN/edge caching, these reads will hit the DB directly and likely overload it at high scale.
findings.fix: Introduce a read-side cache (Redis/Edge cache or CDN caching) for product details, category lists and high-traffic API endpoints. Use stale-while-revalidate, ISR or edge caching for product pages, and cache expensive query results.

evidence.graph: list_flows shows ProductPage flow (criticality 0.565); searchCode found no 'redis' or common cache libraries.

findings.title: Prisma client instantiation pattern not verified (serverless pool risk)
findings.detail: src/lib/prisma.ts imports @prisma/client and is referenced by many API routes. I cannot confirm whether PrismaClient is exported as a long-lived singleton (globalThis.prisma) or instantiated per request because getDependencies failed and schema extraction returned an error. If PrismaClient is constructed per-request in a serverless Next.js deployment, DB connections can be exhausted.
findings.fix: Ensure PrismaClient is exported as a singleton (attach to globalThis in dev) or use an external pooler (PgBouncer/Neon serverless). Configure pool sizes/timeouts appropriate for your platform and add connection telemetry.

evidence.graph: get_file_summary shows import of @prisma/client; searchCode found 'new PrismaClient' only in src/lib/prisma.ts but no 'globalThis.prisma' pattern; getDependencies and getSchemaDefinitions returned errors so instantiation pattern couldn’t be confirmed.

findings.title: Indexes present in migrations but hot-query indexes not fully verified
findings.detail: The repo contains prisma/schema.prisma and many migration SQL files with CREATE INDEX statements indicating indexes exist. However getSchemaDefinitions failed to return parsed schema, so I cannot confirm whether hot-query columns (product.slug, order.userId, cart.userId, coupon.code) have appropriate single or composite indexes for the observed query patterns.
findings.fix: Run schema extraction or EXPLAIN slow queries in the deployed DB to verify indexes on WHERE and JOIN columns used by products, carts and orders. Add composite indexes for frequent multi-column filters as needed.
